# mySSH

> mySSH is a free, open-source desktop SSH client and session manager for macOS, Linux and Windows, written in Rust. It combines saved connection profiles, a tabbed terminal with split panes, an SFTP file panel and one-way folder sync in a single native app.

Latest version: v0.3.0 (2026-10-22, pre-release). License: MIT or Apache-2.0. Author: Alexandro Almeida. Languages: English, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish.

## Features

- **Organized profiles**: Folders, tags, favorites and DEV / STAGING / PRODUCTION environments with a warning stripe. Quick connect without saving anything.
- **Every way to log in**: Password, private key with or without passphrase, SSH agent, keyboard-interactive / MFA and EC2 Instance Connect temporary keys, through jump hosts.
- **Secrets and host keys**: Secrets in Keychain, Credential Manager or Secret Service, never in plain text. Strict host keys: a changed key blocks the connection before anything is sent.
- **AWS EC2 via SSM**: Reach instances with no public IP or open port 22 through Session Manager, without the AWS CLI. AWS profiles or in-app IAM Identity Center sign-in.
- **Tabs and split panes**: A native terminal (alacritty_terminal) with per-profile themes, six palettes and confirmation for multi-line paste.
- **SFTP file panel**: Local and remote side by side, transfer queue, conflict handling, cancellation and resume of large files.
- **Folder sync with preview**: One-way sync that shows every change before it runs. Deletions are off by default and mirror mode is protected.
- **Private by design**: No telemetry and no update checks: the only network traffic is the connections you start. Interface in English, Portuguese and Spanish.

## FAQ

### What is mySSH?

mySSH is a free, open-source desktop SSH client and session manager for macOS, Linux and Windows, written in Rust. It combines saved connection profiles, a tabbed terminal with split panes, an SFTP file panel and one-way folder sync in a single native app.

### Is mySSH free?

Yes. mySSH is free software, dual-licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0. There is no paid edition, no account and no subscription.

### Where does mySSH store passwords and passphrases?

In the operating system's credential vault: Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows and Secret Service on Linux. Secrets are never written in plain text to disk, logs or process arguments.

### Does mySSH support jump hosts, SSH agents and MFA?

Yes. It logs in with a password, a private key (with or without passphrase), the SSH agent or keyboard-interactive authentication, including one-time MFA codes, also through jump hosts (bastions).

### Does mySSH collect any data?

No. There is no telemetry, no account and no automatic update check. The only network connections are the SSH and SFTP sessions you open.

### Is mySSH an alternative to PuTTY or Termius?

Yes. mySSH covers the same everyday work, terminal sessions, saved hosts and file transfer, as a native open-source app that keeps all data on your computer, with no cloud service involved.

### Can mySSH connect to AWS EC2 instances through SSM Session Manager?

Yes. mySSH opens the Session Manager tunnel itself, without the AWS CLI or the session-manager-plugin, so the instance needs no public IP or open port 22. Credentials come from your AWS profiles (~/.aws) or from IAM Identity Center sign-in inside the app, and with EC2 Instance Connect a temporary key is generated on each connection, so nothing has to be set up on the server.
